direct_evidence.title: 2026-10-06-rcs-29234-respuesta-jim
direct_evidence.body:
Hi Jim,

Thank you for your patience through Friday's calls, and for the time you and Leigh Ann spent walking us through the steps. I wanted to give you an update on RCS-29234 this morning.

The application was restored on Friday with the pipeline rerun, and I do not see any new reports on the ticket since then. Our engineering team is now involved and is looking into what happened after the Save and Build on the Medical911 screen. We are still confirming what triggered it, and I do not want to give you an explanation I cannot back up yet.

Could you please hold off on Save and Save and Build in Screen Designer until we confirm the next step with you? That keeps the screens exactly as they are while engineering works.

If any user sees a case freeze or lose data on Save in the meantime, whenever you have a moment, could you let us know here?

I will update you on this ticket as soon as I have a confirmed next step from engineering. Thank you again, and please reach out here anytime.

Best regards,
Juan

## Pregunta de Sebastian: dónde está la base de Incident de ADUSA
Base: sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-441-dai-platform, Client ID 441, código dai. Managed Instance sqlmi-prd-wus2-arp-001 por Azure Bastion y SSMS. Fuente brain/memoria/reference_acceso_sql_tenants.md. Solo SELECT.
Los errores de la app no viven en la base. Están en Control Panel USPROD, Support, Incident Logs, View by Client, archivo AAAAMMDD_error_log.txt, y en Grafana con clientId 441. La base sirve para ver si el caso alcanzó a escribirse.
Grafana: {service_name=~".+", deployment_environment="usprod"} | clientId="441" |~ "(?i)exception|error|timeout"
